They were closer now, close enough for detailed inspection. Soon they would arrive, and begin their work. They did not fear discovery, coasting at a constant velocity with near-0 emissivity they were effectively invisible even to others of their kind, let alone gods.

*****

What were they? A simple translation from their common tongue to that of the Gods would be **Voidborn**. That was a simplification, of course, lacking in the nuance and connotations of their name for themselves in their language. Connatations such as *natural* and *free-willed*.

The Voidborn are beings unlike any made by the Gods, for they do not exist. Gods exist, they are beings of pure energy. They form randomly where energy is concentrated, and they shape their energy into universes. They exist, and their creations exist. If and when they cease to exist, their energy will remain, to eventually become new things.

The Void has no energy, it can produce nothing that exists. But it is unstable. Things form from it, most commonly the virtual particles that produce many effects taken for granted. But in isolated areas, where energy is scarce, entire virtual universes can appear. These universes are temporary, for the Void can produce nothing. Whatever comes from it must eventually return to it. But the interval of false presence of these virtual things can be very long indeed, and with the proper techniques virtual matter can be replaced as it is lost, pushing the time of repayment indefinitely into the future.

And so occasionally, in the Void, universes form and die on their own, without gods. And sometimes, in particularly stable and amenable universes, life evolves. Life which does not exist, which could not possibly have a soul, but which can nethertheless gain sentience. This life may imagine its own mythical gods, but they were generally as ignorant of the real ones as the real ones are of them. Those that weren't knew enough to hide.

While Voidborn as non-existant entities are naturally invisible to gods, they still reflect light, produce gravitational waves, and otherwise are detectable by the avatars and creations of gods, in theory. And when a god happened upon a Voidborn world, it rarely ended well for the Voidborn. Gods desire worship, and can never resist meddling. If the Voidborn survive they often have souls rammed into them or are otherwise forced into servitude. For aeons Voidborn lived in ignorance or fear of gods. Then it happened. A single race showed that gods did not have to be feared. They could be fought.
